thread:
maria: Quick brain dump — want to run a small canary: 5% of EU traffic routed to new 'edge-fast' topology while honoring resident-region pins.

aj: 👍 what's the goal metrics? latency? cold-starts? privacy checks?

maria: main goals: 1) confirm no outbound residency violations, 2) observe KV cache hit-rate when mixing regions, 3) p95 tail latency under 120ms for text-gen requests.

ryan: important: canary must never send user payload outside EU for EU-resident tenants. How are we enforcing that in routing?

maria: plan is proxy-level header hint + routing policy: prefer-local, fallback-to-another-region only if tenant allows. snippet:
```
routing:
  prefer_local: true
  allow_cross_region_fallback: false  # for EU-resident-tenants
  canary_percent: 5
```

sofia: if allow_cross_region_fallback is false, what happens on local capacity exhaustion? 429? degrade to lower model?

maria: fallback policy for resident tenants is strict: 429 + metric emitted. For non-resident opt-in tenants, we allow fallback but annotated in logs for audit.

aj: cache warming concern — mixing requests across regions will fragment KV caches. We should pre-warm common prompt prefixes via a background priming job. ops-runner can you run one?

ops-runner: ops-runner: scheduled priming job queued. Command used: `./prime_cache --region eu --keys-file eu-common-keys.txt --concurrency 10`.

ryan: good. Also add a tracing tag on canary requests: `x-rw-canary: edge-fast-2026-03-21` so we can filter in observability.

maria: yes, will add header and dashboard. aj, can you own alert thresholds? p95>200ms or >1% residency_violations should auto-stop canary.

aj: will do. I'll add a stop-runbook and a deploy-bot hook that tears down canary if thresholds hit.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for edge-fast-2026-03-21 at 1739999999, percent=5.

sofia: quick note — need legal signoff for any telemetry that flags residency candidates. we'll redact sensitive fields before export.

maria: agreed. I'll open a tiny PR for the routing change and link here. thanks everyone — will report back after first 1h sample.
